claims.assertion: This was a RydeTAXI trip, so the metre ran on distance: the fare was $25.81 with a distance component of $13.55 over 9.61 km (F9) at $1.4100/km (F6), and any unjustified extra kilometre was charged to the rider.

The car drove 9.6 km against an optimal 3.9 km, +5.7 km (+144%), and took 26.5 min against an estimated 7.7 min (F1, F3): the driver did not take the shortest and most direct route to Marina Bay Sands.

The GPS records two off-route segments: 14:10–14:15 adding 1.85 km (F4) and 14:17–14:29 adding 2.87 km (F5); together with the fare's billed excess of 5.67 km (F6) these are the unpriced detours behind the extra $7.99 distance charge.

The driver's request at 14:01 named only Cavenagh — 'ok if I go round by Cavenagh?' (F10) — and the rider's reply 'Okay, sure, go ahead' at 14:02 (F11) reached only that named road; nothing in the record places either off-route segment on Cavenagh Road, so the tying evidence required by the policy is absent.

Even accepting the Cavenagh agreement at its widest, the GPS shows 4 min 10 s stationary at 14:20–14:24 at a point 2995 m from the pickup and 2098 m from the drop-off, i.e. not the pickup or the destination (F2) — that halt sits inside the second off-route segment (F5) and is well beyond any permission to pass through Cavenagh.

The rider's own request was only 'Can you stop at a 711 on the way? I need to grab something quick one.' (F11); the rider named no place, and the 4 min 10 s halt at (1.3025, 103.8638) (F2) lies inside the 3.64 km / +2.87 km second segment (F5) that swings far off the optimal route, so the request to 'stop on the way' does not license that route change.

The driver's written statement that he stopped at 'the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road' (F14) is a post-trip claim, not rider consent, and no system record ties either off-route segment to Beach Road — the only stop on record (F2) is not identified by any fact as Beach Road.

The driver's congestion excuse is only half supported: the one incident on record was reported 13:52, 0 m from the optimal route, an accident on Orchard Road towards Bras Basah after Cavenagh Road with two lanes closed (F18), and Orchard Road was speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) only during 14:00–14:10 (F15) — nothing covers the 14:17–14:29 segment, which was 3.64 km at up to 1553 m off the optimal route (F5).

The first off-route segment (14:10–14:15, +1.85 km, F4) overlaps the incident and jam window (F18, F15) and so is the only segment arguably justified; on a strict reading of RD-4(a) the incident was 'after Cavenagh Road', not itself on the segment that leaves Cavenagh, and the 14:17–14:29 segment (F5) is left with no traffic fact at all — the roads in the traffic record (F16, F17) are not shown to be on either detour.

The waiting charge of $1.08 (F7) is a metre waiting unit taken during the 4 min 10 s stop (F2), which is inside the unexplained 14:17–14:29 detour (F5); if that segment is not exempt, the wait it caused is part of the same unexcused deviation.
The detour caused delay and diversion rather than weather conditions: weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain (F19), so no weather excuse is available for the route taken.

The rider has a clean record — 610 days, rating 4.9, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days (F20) — while the driver has 3 disputes and 1 upheld in 90 days (F21); the profile supports asking Ryde to review the account but is not the basis for finding the detour.

weaknesses: The rider did accept the deviation in words: 'Okay, sure, go ahead' at 14:02 (F11) in direct reply to 'ok if I go round by Cavenagh?' (F10), and the first off-route segment starts 14:10 (F4) — after that consent message, so on timing the driver can argue the whole of that segment (and even the loop as one continuous Cavenagh roundabout) was agreed.

The first segment F4 sits squarely inside the incident and jam window — accident on Orchard Road towards Bras Basah after Cavenagh Road at 13:52 (F18) and Orchard Road band 1 (0–9 km/h) 14:00–14:10 (F15) — so the driver has a real RD-4(a) argument for that segment's +1.85 km, and RD-4(b) bands F16/F17 can be cited as corroboration.

The rider did ask for a 7-Eleven stop (F11; complaint confirms a voice message), so the driver will say the 4 min 10 s stop (F2) and the loop that produced it were requested by the rider; the counter is only that the rider named no place (F11) and the stop is 2995 m off the pickup (F2).

The driver's statement (F14) does name Beach Road and a 7-Eleven, which is what the rider's complaint itself acknowledges — 'not a drive out to Beach Road' — so the judge may treat the destination of the second segment as at least identified even though no gps/fare/road-name fact ties F5 to Beach Road.

The metre-based refund is limited: the fare's own distance line is 9.61 km for $13.55 (F9) and the ride was RydeTAXI (policy §0), so the rider cannot recover the fixed platform fee $1.47 or base $3.90 (F9), and any part of the excess kilometrage that the traffic exemption covers (possibly F4) is not refundable.

claims.assertion: The trip began with severe congestion on the optimal route: ORCHARD ROAD recorded speed band 1 (0-9 km/h) at 14:00-14:10, and an LTA-reported accident at 13:52 sat 0 m from the optimal route with two lanes closed, reported before the trip started and inside the trip window.

The driver asked before leaving the optimal route (14:01: 'ok if I go round by Cavenagh?') and the rider expressly agreed at 14:02 ('Okay, sure, go ahead'); that agreement is the rider's own timestamped message predating both off-route segments (which start at 14:10 and 14:17), so segment F4 is a route choice accepted under RD-5/RD-3 and not a deviation.

The rider herself asked in the same message for 'a stop at a 711 on the way', and the car stopped 4 min 10 s at 14:20-14:24 at a point away from pickup and drop-off (F2); a stop the rider's chosen route location accommodates falls to be treated under RD-3 as a rider-requested stop, not a driver errand.

The only waiting charge billed is $1.08 (4.2 min x $0.26/min) matching the 4 min 10 s stop (F2, F7); as this is a RydeTAXI metered trip the waiting time unit is legitimately charged to the rider under RD-3(c) and is not refundable.

The billed excess distance, on the narrowest view of the record, is the mileage of the two off-route segments ($7.99 for 5.67 km at $1.41/km, F6); any refund the judge finds due can only be the mileage of segments it declines to exempt, and the driver does not resist such a partial refund of specific segments.

The chat record is complete - 3 messages, each timestamped (F13) - so the consent question is not one of the G12 evidence-gap cases and the record, not the after-the-fact narrative, governs; the driver's written statement (F14) is not relied on for any finding of consent.

No safety escalation is warranted here: nothing in the chat, the complaint or the driver statement alleges a threat, harassment or a dangerous-driving incident (F10-F14), so SAFE-1 and SAFE-2 are not engaged.

weaknesses: The detour is very large: actual 9.6 km vs 3.9 km optimal (+5.7 km, +144%) and duration 26.5 min vs 7.7 min (F1, F3) - the rider will argue this cannot be explained by a jam on Orchard Road alone.

The rider's agreement (F11) names only Cavenagh and asks for 'a 711 on the way'; no fact in the record places the car on Cavenagh Road or at a 7-Eleven, and F2 places the stop 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off. The rider will use F2/F5 to argue the stop was out at Beach Road and outside the agreed scope, so the judge may find the segment-2 route undetermined (G13) or a driver errand.

The driver's own statement (F14) admits he chose 'the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road' - a location the rider never named - which hands the rider the RD-3(b) argument that the detour to it is unexempted.

Segment 2's traffic support is thin: the only band-1 congestion on record is Orchard Road and it ends at 14:10 (F15), while F5 runs 14:17-14:29; F16 (30-39 km/h) and F17 (20-29 km/h) are not band 1/2 and cannot excuse it under RD-4.
The driver's profile shows 3 disputes and 1 upheld in 90 days (F21), which the rider will cite to invite a flag_account under RD-6 if any part of the case is upheld.

points.response: The congestion and accident are real but time- and place-limited: Orchard Road band 1 runs only 14:00-14:10 (F15) and the accident was 'on Orchard Road (towards Bras Basah) after Cavenagh Road' at 13:52 (F18), so they can explain at most a reroute off Orchard in the first minutes and say nothing about 14:17-14:29, when 3.64 km were driven with up to 1553 m off the optimal route (F5).

Conceded as to scope: the rider's own 14:02 message 'Okay, sure, go ahead' (F11) answered the driver's 14:01 ask naming Cavenagh (F10) and predates the first segment (F4), so F4 is an agreed named-road route choice; but under RD-5 and G13 that agreement reaches only driving on Cavenagh Road, and no fact ties F4 (or F5) to Cavenagh Road - no traffic fact even mentions Cavenagh (F15-F18).

The rider named no place, only 'a stop at a 711 on the way' (F11), and the only stop on record sits 2995 m from the pickup and 2098 m from the drop-off (F2), inside the second off-route segment (F5), so under RD-3(b) the route change that reached it is not exempted by the request to stop on the way.

Conceded on the metre: on a RydeTAXI trip waiting units are chargeable (RD-3(c)) and the billed $1.08 for 4.2 min at $0.26/min matches the 4 min 10 s stop (F7, F2); I do not ask for the waiting unit back.

The driver's own $4.05 figure prices only F4's 1.85 km (F4) at the trip rate $1.4100/km (F6) and abandons F5's 2.87 km (F5), even though the stop the rider did request (F2) lies inside F5 and no traffic fact covers 14:17-14:29 (F15-F18); the correct refund on the unmatched kilometrage is $6.46 (4.58 km x $1.4100/km, per F4, F5, F6).

I accept the chat record is complete (F13), and that is precisely why the driver's post-trip Beach Road account (F14) cannot supply consent: RD-5 requires the rider's own message before the segment, and no rider message before 14:17 places the car on Beach Road or names that 7-Eleven.

I do not withdraw C1: the fare record shows a distance line of $13.55 over 9.61 km (F9) at $1.4100/km (F6), so the kilometrage the driver does not resist refunding was genuinely charged to the rider under RD-2.

Accepted as far as it goes: this is a metered RydeTAXI trip and the distance line is $13.55 for 9.61 km at $1.4100/km (F9, F6), so the refund measure is extra kilometrage only — which is why the driver's brief asks at most for the mileage of segments the judge declines to exempt (D5).

The raw totals are not in dispute (F1, F3), but the obligation in RD-1 is qualified by 'in the absence of any reasonable cause to do otherwise', and here the reasonable cause is on record: Orchard Road speed band 1 (0-9 km/h) at 14:00-14:10 and a two-lane-closure accident 0 m from the optimal route reported 13:52 (F15, F18).

The two segments are on record (F4, F5), but the fare's 5.67 km billed excess (F6) is not the same quantity as the 4.72 km summed from the segments (1.85 + 2.87), so the rider overstates the recoverable base; only the exempted-or-not segment mileage can be refunded under RD-2.

No system record ties either segment to Cavenagh Road, so the driver does not claim the segment is tied to that named road; the rider's own yes at 14:02 (F11) still operates as her authorisation for the loop she was told about at 14:01 (F10), and it predates both segments (F4, F5).

The 4 min 10 s halt at 14:20-14:24, 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off (F2), sits inside the second segment (F5) and is exactly the stop the rider asked for in the same message that gave the go-ahead (F11), so it is a rider-requested stop under RD-3, not a driver's own excursion; the driver nonetheless concedes the loop that produced it is not tied to the named road Cavenagh.

The rider did ask for a stop 'on the way' without naming a place (F11), and the driver as a matter of policy could not pick a location that took the car off the corridor without telling her; the driver therefore does not resist the second segment's kilometrage being treated as unexempt (D5) — but the stop itself was requested and the metered wait it caused stays chargeable under RD-3(c).

Accepted: the Beach Road reference exists only in the driver's post-trip statement (F14), no gps/fare/road-name fact ties either segment to Beach Road, and the driver relies on no post-trip narrative for any finding (D6).

The $1.08 billed is 4.2 min x $0.26/min (F7) matching the 4 min 10 s rider-requested stop (F2), and on a RydeTAXI trip the meter's waiting unit for a stop is chargeable under RD-3(c) irrespective of whether the segment mileage is exempted.
Fair weather (F19) rules out no excuse the driver ever raised: the driver's case rests on the recorded accident and the Orchard Road band-1 congestion (F18, F15), not on weather.

The driver's profile (3 disputes, 1 upheld, of which 0 route upsets, F21) is exactly the kind of fact the policy says may support only an additional account-review action, and cannot decide the route question; the rider's clean record (F20) does not fill the two-point gap between 4.72 km of segment mileage (F4, F5) and the 5.67 km billed (F6).
